blocks.content: PFRDA faces the critical challenge of expanding pension coverage to India's vast unorganized workforce while balancing market-linked returns with long-term fund security.

rows: Fixed investment managed as per government guidelines

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Low pension coverage in India's vast unorganized workforce remains a major structural challenge for PFRDA.
Widespread lack of financial literacy and pension awareness hinders voluntary adoption of the National Pension System (NPS).
Balancing market-linked investment risks with subscriber demand for security and stable long-term retirement yields.
Competition from traditional, guaranteed-return small savings instruments like EPF and Public Provident Fund (PPF).
Strengthening regulatory oversight over Pension Fund Managers (PFMs), Point of Presence (PoPs), and Central Recordkeeping Agencies (CRAs).
PFRDA was established as a statutory body under the PFRDA Act, 2013, which came into force in February 2014.
Unlike EPF which is a defined benefit model, NPS is a defined contribution pension system regulated by PFRDA.
PFRDA consists of a Chairperson and up to six members (at least three whole-time) appointed by the Central Government.
